name: Tautulli (Plex statistics)
param_style: ? positional (python sqlite3); SQL assembled with %-formatting and the DataTables column/join/where builder, some literals inlined
schema_source: plexpy/__init__.py dbcheck() CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX statements (only the tables the queries use); fetched, not vendored (GPL)
data_scale: scale 1: 135k session_history rows over 4 years (~200 plays/day in the last month) with 1:1 session_history_metadata and session_history_media_info, 40 users (5 heavy users hold 70 % of plays; 3 archived, 1 deleted), 8 library sections (1 archived, 1 deleted), 3000 movies / 400 shows / 800 artists with Zipf-like popularity, 1 play in 7 grouped with the previous one, 4 live sessions; about 150 MB
visibility_note: 6.6k stars; the standard monitoring companion for Plex Media Server, shipped in every NAS app store (Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS); SQLite is its only database
interest_note: History page: a 55-column GROUP BY reference_id over a 3-table LEFT JOIN with UNION ALL of live sessions, ORDER BY a COLLATE NOCASE alias and LIMIT/OFFSET, pruned by an IN (subquery) page bound or a six-way LIKE search bound, counted with COUNT(*) OVER (); graphs and home stats are two-level GROUP BYs (per play, then per day/hour/user/title) with CASE sums and localtime date bucketing.
reach_note: widely self-hosted alongside Plex; SQLite is the only backend

cpu_evidence.summary: history page query ~20 s at 350k session_history rows (572k rows / 1.8 GB also reported); home stats ~70 s for a 30-user server; whole grouped 3-table join materialised before pagination
moved datatables pagination into SQL (LIMIT/OFFSET + separate COUNT over the inner query): page 1 0.41 -> 0.29 s at 35k rows, but searches got 17 % slower and slow-disk users saw regressions
filtered count folded into the page query with COUNT(*) OVER (); maintainer merged an alternative (page bound + cheap count) on nightly: history page change 3.5 s -> 2.5 s on an Unraid box
